```python
from itertools import permutations

# Adjective classes; nouns do not impose adjective-order constraints.
classes = {
    "opinion": "nice wonderful good lovely obnoxious mysterious silly awful terrible "
               "ridiculous repulsive",
    "purpose": "whittling drinking hiking snorkeling typing exercise eating smoking "
               "walking driving",
    "size": "massive enormous big huge midsize small tiny medium-size normal-size "
            "large little",
    "color": "gray brown yellow indigo blue violet green maroon black red aqua teal "
             "cyan crimson pink",
    "age": "ancient archaic new old-fashioned brand-new old",
    "shape": "spherical pyramidal circular square prismlike rectangular triangular",
    "material": "cardboard glass steel fiberglass iron cloth wool plastic rubber "
                "wood paper",
    "origin": "indian vietnamese turkish russian egyptian thai bangladeshi congolese "
              "iranian american ethiopian indonesian pakistani mexican filipino japanese",
}
category = {
    word: name
    for name, words in classes.items()
    for word in words.split()
}

# Every given sentence containing multiple adjectives, with its noun removed.
# Single-adjective examples impose no relative-order constraint.
examples = [
    "good gray archaic",
    "massive yellow",
    "good drinking",
    "big maroon",
    "enormous violet",
    "glass vietnamese",
    "lovely snorkeling",
    "ancient spherical",
    "old-fashioned spherical",
    "brand-new square",
    "good typing",
    "silly exercise",
    "steel turkish",
    "iron russian",
    "silly snorkeling",
    "huge green",
    "steel thai",
    "brand-new circular",
    "brand-new pyramidal",
    "huge indigo",
    "midsize black",
    "wonderful whittling",
    "steel bangladeshi",
    "wool iranian",
    "ancient rectangular",
    "plastic thai",
    "big black",
    "rubber russian",
    "iron ethiopian",
    "normal-size teal",
    "ridiculous typing",
    "small cyan",
    "huge yellow",
    "awful whittling",
    "old prismlike",
    "silly whittling",
    "terrible smoking",
    "huge crimson",
    "old-fashioned pyramidal",
    "old triangular",
    "ancient spherical",
    "nice snorkeling",
    "big maroon",
    "ancient circular",
    "driving midsize rectangular",
    "steel russian",
    "terrible hiking",
    "large crimson",
    "brand-new spherical",
    "fiberglass indian",
    "normal-size maroon",
]

options = {
    "A": "nice typing big yellow new rectangular wool",
    "B": "silly whittling little gray archaic square vietnamese",
    "C": "mexican medium-size violet ancient spherical typing silly",
    "D": "plastic large blue old-fashioned rectangular whittling good",
    "E": "wood turkish tiny pink archaic prismlike whittling",
    "F": "silly hiking medium-size black old-fashioned spherical mexican steel",
    "G": "terrible eating midsize green brand-new prismlike",
    "H": "filipino paper small violet new spherical snorkeling",
    "I": "snorkeling little brown old circular plastic american",
    "J": "japanese glass midsize aqua brand-new spherical",
}

def categories(text):
    return tuple(category[word] for word in text.split())

# Include every earlier/later pair, not merely adjacent adjectives.
constraints = set()
for example in examples:
    sequence = categories(example)
    for i, earlier in enumerate(sequence):
        for later in sequence[i + 1:]:
            assert earlier != later
            constraints.add((earlier, later))

option_categories = {
    letter: categories(text) for letter, text in options.items()
}

# Exhaustively test all 8! class orders against all observations.
valid_orders = []
answer_sets = set()
witnesses = {}
for order in permutations(classes):
    position = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(order)}
    if not all(position[a] < position[b] for a, b in constraints):
        continue

    valid_orders.append(order)
    correct = []
    for letter, sequence in option_categories.items():
        if all(position[a] < position[b]
               for a, b in zip(sequence, sequence[1:])):
            correct.append(letter)
            witnesses.setdefault(letter, order)
    answer_sets.add("".join(correct) or "K")

if not valid_orders:
    print("UNSUPPORTED: the class-order model contradicts the observations.")
    print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
else:
    possible = "".join(letter for letter in options if letter in witnesses)
    guaranteed = "".join(
        letter for letter in options
        if all(letter in answer for answer in answer_sets)
    )
    print("Exhaustively examined 40320 class-order permutations.")
    print("Orders satisfying every supplied constraint:", len(valid_orders))
    print("Choices compatible with the observations:", possible)
    print("Choices correct under every consistent class order:", guaranteed)
    print("Possible complete answer strings:", ", ".join(sorted(answer_sets)))

    intended_order = (
        "opinion", "purpose", "size", "color",
        "age", "shape", "material", "origin"
    )
    assert intended_order in valid_orders
    p = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(intended_order)}
    intended_answer = "".join(
        letter for letter, sequence in option_categories.items()
        if all(p[a] < p[b] for a, b in zip(sequence, sequence[1:]))
    ) or "K"
    print("Answer under the intended full ordering:", intended_answer)

    # Even if the observations leave some class placements unspecified,
    # G is correct in every consistent ordering, decisively ruling out K.
    submitted = "K"
    if submitted not in answer_sets:
        print("CHECK FAIL")
    elif answer_sets == {submitted}:
        print("CHECK PASS")
    else:
        print("UNSUPPORTED: observations do not uniquely determine the submission.")
        print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
```
